calls.head: The Hurricanes will send their checkers at Bolduc
calls.body: At home, the Hurricanes keep sending Jarvis’s line (Martinook, Staal and Jarvis) out against opponents’ second lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Rod Brind'Amour has been using this group as a checking line on opponents’ second lines. Tonight the Canadiens’ second line is Bolduc, Danault and Texier.

calls.head: Stay out of the box, Canadiens
calls.body: The Hurricanes’ power play is one of the league’s best, and the Canadiens’ kill is near the bottom. The Canadiens need to stay out of the box. The Canadiens take a lot of penalties and the Hurricanes draw plenty of them, so their power play should get its chances.

CAR.head: We gave Carolina an 81% chance, but Montréal had other ideas.

MTL.head: We gave Montréal only a 19% chance, and they proved us wrong.

surprises.head: Montréal shortened their bench
surprises.body: Montréal’s bottom-six forwards played 33% of the forwards’ 5-on-5 time, against their usual 43% and a league average of 42%. A team strays this far about once every 600 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

surprises.head: Montréal picked Carolina’s defense apart
surprises.body: Carolina usually gives up some of the league’s most dangerous shots. Even by those standards, this was a night of good looks: Montréal’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 9.5% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.5% (about 7.2% against Carolina) and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far about once every 20 games.

story.head: Hutson ties it late and wins it in overtime
paras: Taylor Hall and Kaiden Guhle fought early in the third, and Nikolaj Ehlers got the scoring started for the Hurricanes with a little over six minutes left. Lane Hutson made it 1-1 for Montréal with just under five minutes left. He won it with his second goal of the night 38 seconds into overtime.

Nothing much separated these two on the chances. This one could have gone either way. The Hurricanes hit two posts and still lost. Jakub Dobeš made 26 saves for the Canadiens, and Pyotr Kochetkov kept the Canes in it, stopping 22 of 24. The Canadiens moved to 14-5-4 and climbed to second in the Atlantic, while the Hurricanes fell to 16-3-3, still first in the NHL in points percentage.
